intent.quote: Also increase the timeout for all hooks
intent.readback: plumb's model work runs in the background so the agent carries on, within time limits you can change by asking, and those limits may be larger than today's so a hook is cut only when it is truly stuck. When work takes a while, a small mod shows an animated progress bar saying what plumb is doing, and no background process opens a window. Keeping the agent's context small and never blocking on plumb's own failure are no longer requirements of yours; the agent still gets each record once and a short brief, as you asked earlier (INT-016).
will: Run reading and judging as batched background jobs through one dispatcher, so no hook waits on a model.
Start every background process on Windows with no console window, outliving the hook that started it.
Keep every hook time limit a setting with generous defaults (watchdog 30 s, soft budgets 20 s and 5 s, covering tests 60 s per turn), changed when you ask in plain words and allowed to grow.
Show long work as an animated progress bar with a plain-words message in plumb's small band in Claude Code (P12's progress requirement).
Give the agent each relevant record once per session through one emitter, with a short session brief.
wont: Make "keeps the agent's context small" or "never blocks the owner's work on its own failure" a requirement of this principle; the once-per-session emitter and the short brief stay as agent-facing behaviour carried from confirmed INT-016.
Fix the limits at today's values, or ask you to edit configuration files or type a command to change them.
Fall back to word rules when a model is unreachable.
Show progress for hook runs that finish within their budget, or invent estimates when the total is unknown.
Install the Claude Code mod for other hosts.
assumptions: The owner sets a limit by asking in plain words; the agent writes it to .plumb/config.yaml (P2).
A hook's internal error or a job that never settles goes to the debug workflow (P5), in place of a promise never to block.
The once-per-session emitter and the short brief stay as agent-facing behaviour backed by confirmed examples (INT-016), though P13 no longer states "context small" as the owner's requirement.

INT-072's quote covers the time limits; the background jobs, the no-window launch and the progress display rest on P13 as confirmed, the emitter and brief on INT-016. Progress is one requirement, P12's.

requirements.title: plumb's model work runs as batched background jobs
requirements.statement: Reading the owner's answers and judging records run as background jobs: hooks queue them, batched one per turn or per capture, and a background worker runs them through the one configured dispatcher, recomputing each job's inputs from the logs, so no hook waits on a model. Clarifying runs only inside the intent loop (P6). A failing job says so, settles nothing and is retried at the next turn end, up to 3 attempts; after the third it goes to P5's debug workflow. There is no rule-based fallback.

examples.given: the last reply showed something for the owner to answer, and the owner's message arrives
examples.then: it queues the read job and returns within its time limit without waiting for the model

examples.given: the Claude Code dispatcher runs a job
examples.when: plumb's hooks fire inside that headless session
examples.then: they exit at once and queue nothing

examples.given: the configured model is unreachable
examples.then: the turn-end plumb line says plumb could not check the owner's answers, nothing is approved, and the job is retried next turn

examples.given: the same job inputs queued twice
examples.then: the job runs once

examples.given: the configured model is unreachable
examples.when: the worker runs the read job
examples.then: no word rule decides in the model's place and nothing is approved

examples.given: the Claude Code dispatcher builds its command
examples.then: the command selects the plumb agent with --agent and passes --setting-sources empty, --strict-mcp-config and --disable-slash-commands, runs in an empty temporary directory, and the job's context holds no CLAUDE.md text

examples.given: a judge job queued by the agent through plumb capture, with inputs that differ from the logs
examples.then: the worker uses the inputs it recomputed from the logs, not the file's, so the file cannot make a record look supported

examples.given: a turn whose previous reply showed five records and one open question
examples.then: one read job covers all six items, not six jobs

examples.given: a capture that writes one intent and six requirements
examples.then: one judge job is queued for the seven records

examples.given: a job that has failed at three turn ends in a row
examples.then: the plumb line says one case went to debugging, and the job is not queued again by the turn end

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live Claude Code session the owner answers a question and keeps working; the agent carries on at once while the band shows plumb reading the answer, and the next plumb line says what the read found; the job ledger shows one read job for the turn.

requirements.title: Background processes open no window and outlive the hook that started them
requirements.statement: Every background process plumb starts goes through one launch helper: on Windows with no console window (CREATE_NO_WINDOW with a new process group, never a detached process), for it and for the commands it runs; on macOS and Linux in its own session. It keeps running after the hook that started it exits.

examples.given: a Windows machine
examples.when: the stop hook starts the understand worker
examples.then: no console window appears for the worker nor for the commands it runs

examples.given: a Windows machine
examples.then: no console window appears for it nor for its git and pytest calls

examples.given: the hook that started a background process has exited
examples.then: it keeps running to the end of its work

examples.given: macOS or Linux
examples.then: it starts in its own session, as before

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live Claude Code session on this Windows machine the owner works through a turn that starts the worker and the background test map; no console window opens at any point.

requirements.title: Hook time limits are generous settings the owner can raise
requirements.statement: Every time limit around plumb's hooks (the watchdog's hard limit, each hook's soft budget, a turn's covering-test budget, the judge's and git's time inside a hook) is a setting whose default is generous enough that a hook is cut only when truly stuck. The owner changes a limit by asking in plain words, and limits may grow past today's, up to what the plugin's fixed host hook timeouts allow.

examples.given: a loaded machine where a hook takes 4 s to answer
examples.when: the hook runs with the default settings
examples.then: it is not cut and its check is not skipped

examples.given: a hook that never answers
examples.then: the watchdog cuts it with the budget notice, at the configured value

examples.given: .plumb/config.yaml sets hooks.hard_limit_s and hooks.budget_ms
examples.then: the watchdog and the budgets use those values, and the defaults apply when unset

examples.given: the default hard limit plus the stop hook's grace
examples.when: the host hook timeouts are read from the plugin bundle
examples.then: every one of them is above that sum

examples.given: the owner says "let the hooks run up to 45 seconds"
examples.then: the hard limit becomes 45 s in .plumb/config.yaml and the next hook is cut only after 45 s; the owner typed no command

examples.given: the owner asks for hooks to run up to two minutes, above the plugin's 60 s host hook timeouts
examples.then: the hard limit is set to 59 s, the most the host timeouts allow with the stop hook's 1 s grace, and the agent tells the owner the host would cut a longer hook first

examples.given: plumb's own repository
examples.when: each hook runs as a subprocess
examples.then: each finishes within its configured budget

examples.given: a settled line and a question to show at the end of a turn
examples.then: the turn-end plumb line is produced within the stop budget

examples.given: a hook raises an internal error
examples.then: it writes the error to the session error log, exits 0 so the host goes on, and the plumb line says one case went to debugging

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: a hook test drives each hook with a scripted 4 s delay (not cut, check not skipped) and with a hang (cut at the configured hard limit with the budget notice); then, in a live session, the owner asks in plain words for a longer limit and sees the agent apply it and the plugin's host timeouts stay above it.

requirements.title: The post-edit hook records each edited path for the turn
requirements.statement: After each edit the post-edit hook adds the edited path to the session's touched list, which the turn's staleness, trace and covering-test checks read, and exits 0.

examples.given: an agent edits src/plumb/links.py
examples.then: the path is recorded in the session's touched list and the hook exits 0

examples_dropped.why: P13 drops "never blocks the owner's work on its own failure" as a requirement; a hook's own failure is now the internal-error example of the time-limit requirement, routed to the debug workflow (P5)

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: a hook test edits a file under a scratch session and shows the path in the session's touched list.

requirements.title: The agent gets each relevant record once per session
requirements.statement: Every agent-facing line from plumb's hooks and API passes through one emitter that gives the agent each relevant record once per session, again only when its hash or state changes or after a /clear or compaction, never cuts a must or one-shot line, and points to plumb show for details.

examples.given: 10 prompts about the same three unchanged records
examples.when: the prompt hook runs each time
examples.then: each record's line is injected once

examples.given: an untraced-change instruction already emitted for src/app/mul.py
examples.when: the next prompt hook runs with the path still untraced
examples.then: the instruction is not repeated

examples.given: SR-004 changed after its line was injected
examples.then: its line is injected once more with the new state

examples.given: a queued untraced-change instruction for src/app/mul.py, whose note the hook consumes when it reads it, and relevant records that fill hooks.prompt_tokens
examples.then: the instruction is injected all the same; a one-shot line (queued instruction or escalation) is never cut by the budget

examples.given: the owner types the same words ("continue", "ok") in two turns of one session
examples.when: each turn's stop finds covering tests without fresh evidence
examples.then: each turn blocks once with the covering-tests instruction; a per-turn line is deduplicated within its turn, never for the whole session

examples.given: a session whose first prompt injected "SR-003 [proposed] Links pin both ends"
examples.when: a second prompt names SR-003 again and nothing changed
examples.then: the hook injects nothing; another session still gets the line

examples.given: the same session
examples.when: SR-003's statement is edited and a prompt names SR-003 and SR-004
examples.then: only the SR-003 line is injected again

examples.given: SR-004 injected as proposed
examples.when: it is approved (by the judge or the owner's answer) and a prompt names it
examples.then: "SR-004 [approved]" is injected once with the compare line, and not on the next prompt

examples.given: a prompt budget that fits one line and a prompt naming SR-003 and SR-004
examples.then: the first injects SR-003 and points to plumb show SR-004, which is not marked as given; the second injects SR-004 only

examples.given: SR-003 already given this session
examples.when: the owner runs /clear or the context is compacted
examples.then: the next prompt naming SR-003 injects its line again

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: a hook test runs ten prompts naming the same three records in one session and shows each line injected once, re-injected after an edit and after /clear.

requirements.title: The session brief is about 30 lines, compact by default
requirements.statement: plumb brief names the features, intents, records not yet approved, drift, decisions and open NCs in about 30 lines (cap 40), naming records rather than procedures; the session start injects its compact form by default: a few lines of counts, open NCs and a pointer.

examples.given: a repository with 60 intents and 30 open NCs
examples.then: it prints at most 30 lines and ends the long lists with "+N more (plumb brief --all)"

examples.given: a repository with FEAT-001, INT-001 and proposed SR-001
examples.then: it names FEAT-001, INT-001 and SR-001 as not yet approved

examples.given: 60 intents and 5 open NCs
examples.then: the compact brief is at most 6 lines, with counts, open NCs and a pointer, and lists no intent title

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: plumb brief on a repository of 60 intents prints at most 30 lines, and a session start there shows at most 6 lines.

decisions.question: Which Windows creation flags do background plumb processes use?
decisions.chosen: CREATE_NO_WINDOW with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, never DETACHED_PROCESS, through one launch helper shared by every background process.
alternatives: Keep DETACHED_PROCESS and add CREATE_NO_WINDOW to every one of the 50 subprocess calls plumb makes.
Keep DETACHED_PROCESS and accept the windows.

decisions.question: How long may a hook run before it is cut?
decisions.chosen: Watchdog hard limit 30 s; soft budgets 20 s (session start, prompt, stop) and 5 s (post-edit); covering tests 60 s per turn; judge in a hook 5 s; git in the stop hook 5 s; host timeouts 60 s and 120 s, kept above the hard limit plus the stop grace. All are settings the owner may raise by asking.
alternatives: 6 s hard limit with 4 s soft budgets, accepting skipped checks.
Remove the watchdog and rely on the host timeouts alone.

retired_decisions.why: matters false; its rule (a session brief of about 30 lines, cap 40) is stated by the context requirement
